title: Liability and Contributions of New Citizens to National Service
what_it_is: Liability and Contributions of New Citizens to National Service

sections.label: New citizens and NS enlistment
sections.summary: Since 2000, about 3,400 new citizens are registered yearly and are liable for NS, though mature adult citizens are not enlisted.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Since 2000, on average, 3,400 new citizens are registered each year, who have been or will be enlisted like all male Singaporeans to serve their NS duties.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: I quote in full MINDEF's reply: "Under the Enlistment Act, all male Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents between the ages of 18 and 40 for non-officers and 50 for officers are liable to serve National Service (NS).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: However, males who receive citizenship as mature adults, typically in their 30s and 40s, are not enlisted as they are not suitable for full-time NS at that age and did not enjoy any benefits prior to their citizenship.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: New male citizens who stayed in Singapore when young and enjoyed economic and social benefits are enlisted when they reach 18 years of age or older.

sections.label: NSF share of new citizens and PRs
sections.summary: New citizens and PRs rose from about 5% of full-time NSFs in the early 2000s to about 20% today, slightly more than half being citizens by registration.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: In the early 2000s, they were about 5% of all full-time national servicemen (NSFs) enlisted each year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Today, they form about 20% of all NSFs enlisted.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Of the 20%, slightly more than half are citizens by registration, with the remaining as PRs.

sections.label: Full facts on NS enlistees
sections.summary: He stated that new citizens and PRs form 20% of full-time NS enlistees, with more than half being male new citizens and the rest PRs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: I gave him all of the full facts.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: I said they form 20% of full-time NS enlistees, of which more than half are male new citizens while the rest are PRs.

sections.label: Dispute over new citizen numbers
sections.summary: He said the other was avoiding debate, citing the 3,400 average new citizens and PRs enlisted yearly and a 10% new citizen figure of 1,700.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: And now, he is running away from the debate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: He told me, through my Parliamentary Question last month and he said again just now, that there were 3,400 new citizens and PRs who enlisted every year, on the average.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: So, if he says 10% of that is new citizens, that would be 1,700.

sections.label: Clarification on new citizens' NS
sections.summary: He repeated that since 2000 about 3,400 new citizens are registered yearly and added that new citizens and PRs form about 20% of NSmen.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Since 2000, on average, 3,400 new citizens are registered each year, who have been or will be enlisted like all male Singaporeans to serve their NS duties.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: I further added today that new citizens and PRs form about 20% of all NSmen enlisted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: My clarification is: what is the number of new citizens who have not performed NS?
